                    The hairy cell leukemia (hairy cell leukemia) presents as characteristic clinical-biological features:

Lymphocytosis is common, but counts greater than 50,000 lymphocytes/microL are not typical; instead, lymphocyte counts are often elevated but usually less than this threshold. The presence of T lymphoid line markers is indeed a key diagnostic feature, confirming the diagnosis. Pancytopenia and splenomegaly are also common presentations in hairy cell leukemia, aligning with the consensus that these findings are typical. Exfoliative generalized erythroderma is not typical for hairy cell leukemia and may indicate a misdiagnosis.
